newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK interbank market up on hopes of U.S. rate hike.
newsitem.headline: HK interbank market up on hopes of U.S. rate hike.

text.p: Hong Kong's interbank market received a strong boost on Wednesday on optimism of an interest rate hike in the United States, dealers said.
The overnight stood at 5-1/16 1/4 percent against 5.0 percent on Tuesday, while three months stood at 5-3/4 11/16 percent versus 5-1/2 7/16 percent.
"Rates are much higher because of the possibility of a quarter percent hike in (U.S.) interest rates," a dealer with a Japanese bank said.
The optimism, however, battered bills and notes as jittery players moved to the side to wait for an official decision on U.S. interest rates on September 24.
"People are quite afraid and would rather stay sidelined to wait for results and other fresh news," a local dealer said.
"It's risky to take positions now," she said.

The one-week bill yielded 5.00 percent against Tuesday's 4.87 percent while the seven-year Exchange Fund note yielded 7.60 percent against 7.57 percent, five-year 7.30 percent versus 7.24 percent and three-year 6.65 percent versus 6.59 percent.
